description: Content format × channel registry — the leaf-level vocabulary the suggestor uses to specify HOW an idea ships. Each format declares the channels it can run on, production complexity, evidence requirements, and which strategies/journey-stages it fits best. The LLM proposer is constrained to ids in this file; new formats must be added here before they can be referenced by generated content_suggestions.
notes: format_class groups formats by mode (narrative / explainer / tool / event / community). Used for filtering in the UI.
production_complexity is qualitative: low (hours, no production), medium (days, light production), high (weeks, full production with consent/legal/medical review).

evidence_requirement names the kind of patient evidence the format demands. 'consented_quote' means a real patient quote with documented consent; 'composite_archetype' means a synthesized persona, not a real person.
best_for_strategies and best_for_stages let the mapping layer score format candidates by intersection with the chosen strategy + journey context.

items.label: Long-form explainer article
items.description: 1500-3500 word indexable explainer optimized for organic search. Anchors the SEO strategy and works as the canonical reference other formats link back to.

items.label: Short explainer video (60-180s)
items.description: Short, motion-graphic or simple-talking-head video explaining one concept clearly. Pairs well with long-form explainers as a top-of-funnel hook.

items.label: Patient-story video (3-8 min)
items.description: Documentary-style first-person video. High emotional payoff; high consent, legal, and production cost. Anchor format for MG United / More Than MG playbook.

items.label: First-person essay
items.description: Written first-person essay. Lower production cost than video, easier to syndicate via advocacy newsletters, and indexable for SEO when the headline matches search demand.

items.label: Podcast episode (host-and-guest)
items.description: 30-60 min conversational episode. Strong fit for partnerships with advocacy podcasts already in-market (e.g., Kaleidoscope Fighting Lupus's podcast, GHLF's Talking Head Pain network).

items.label: Decision-aid worksheet
items.description: Printable / fillable worksheet that walks a patient through a structured decision (e.g., 'questions to ask your nephrologist before starting voclosporin', 'is a CAR-T trial right for you'). High utility per artifact.

items.label: Interactive symptom / trial-eligibility checker
items.description: Web-based tool that routes the user through a question tree to a recommendation (see a rheumatologist / explore these trials). Requires medical review, ongoing maintenance, and clear non-diagnostic disclaimers.

items.label: Static infographic / visual explainer
items.description: Single-image visual explainer. Highly shareable in patient social communities; works as a recurring volume play around an awareness month or campaign launch.

items.label: Reddit AMA / community Q&A
items.description: Hosted Q&A with a clinician, researcher, or trial-experienced patient. Surfaces unanswered questions verbatim, useful as input back into future explainer content. Requires careful pre-coordination with subreddit moderators.

items.label: Co-branded advocacy webinar
items.description: Live or recorded webinar co-produced with an advocacy partner. Borrows the partner's audience, branding, and editorial credibility.

items.label: Search-optimized landing page
items.description: Tight landing page targeting one search-intent cluster (e.g., 'is fatigue a sign of lupus nephritis'). Often paired with a long-form explainer as the canonical destination.

items.label: Caregiver guide
items.description: PDF or web guide aimed at the partner / parent / adult child carrying logistical and emotional load. Often the highest-utility format for trial-consideration phases because the caregiver is the decision-influencer.

items.label: Financial / payer-navigation worksheet
items.description: Structured worksheet covering prior-auth letters, copay programs, foundation grants, and appeal scripts. Typically co-produced with American Kidney Fund or similar.

items.label: HCP CME module
items.description: Accredited continuing-medical-education module for clinicians (PCPs, rheumatologists, nephrologists). Long production cycle and regulatory overhead; high credibility ceiling.

items.label: Peer-mentor matching program
items.description: Structured 1-1 matching between a newly-diagnosed or trial-considering patient and a trained peer mentor. High ongoing operational cost; rare and high-trust when done well.

items.label: Short social post (Instagram / TikTok / X)
items.description: Short-form social content. High velocity, low individual stakes; works as the surface that drives traffic to higher-investment formats.

items.label: Clinic / point-of-care handout
items.description: Printable one- or two-pager designed for handing to a patient at the end of a visit. Often the most-used artifact in clinic workflows and the easiest to get past medical-affairs review.
